item.title: Spicy Baked Marinated Tofu
item.description: Marinate tofu in a mix of rice vinegar, peanut butter, ketchup, garlic, and soy sauce, and discover that tofu really can be tasty!

item.title: Pan Seared Tuna with Citrus-Herb Vinaigrette
item.description: A more modern version of Salade Nicoise with an Asian influence that can be eaten as an entree. Salmon, halibut, or snapper also go well in this dish.

item.title: Macaroni and Cheese with Ham, Peas and Shallots
item.description: Macaroni and cheese is perfect supper food. It's a kids' favorite, and adults like it too. My recipe is simple and almost as quick as the boxed variety. Try this variation with ham, peas and shallots.

item.title: Chicken Teriyaki Crispy Rice
item.description: This pan fried crispy rice topped with teriyaki chicken is a fun snack or appetizer.

item.title: Apricot Chops
item.description: What do you get when you cross simple with delicious? Apricot Chops, of course! Simply choose your favorite vegetable or rice as an accompaniment, pop them in the oven, and enjoy this sweet and savory delight!

item.title: Pluots and Pork
item.description: This is a quick dinner idea, featuring thin pork chops simmered in a sauce made of white wine and fresh, in-season stone fruit. Try it with plums or apricots if pluots aren't available.

item.title: Central American Tacos
item.description: Wonderful authentic tacos I first tasted in Guatemala at a taco stand. May be a little different to the American taste, but the green sauce is the crowning touch. The flavors are the subtle flavors of Central America.

item.title: Sweet Asian Short Ribs
item.description: Loquat preserves and sweet chile sauce deliver a special and unique flavor to these slow-cooked Asian-style beef short ribs.

item.title: BBQ Pork Crispy Rice
item.description: Crispy BBQ flavored rice, cheese, and BBY pulled pork come together in this delicious appetizer or main dish.

item.title: Chicken Cilantro
item.description: Don't let the color scare you! It's bright green! This is an extremely easy and tasty family recipe. Variations can definitely be made to taste...sometimes I use chicken (boneless or not) sometimes I use shrimp...sometimes I use both. My family makes it with chicken innards (gizzards, heart, etc.) which I'm not too keen on eating. Hey, but with this soup it's to each his or her own.
